title: Hotpatch triage matrix, severity criteria, and automated patch propagation scripts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Consolidate severity criteria for hotpatches, formalize a triage matrix used by on-call and release engineers, and deliver a small set of scripts that automate safe propagation of critical fixes across supported release branches (main, stable-X.Y, lts-X.Y). This ticket scopes the policy, gating tests, branch naming conventions, and the initial automation prototypes for one-click propagation with built-in verification and rollback hooks.
problem_statement: Current hotpatches are handled ad-hoc: engineers manually create patch branches, backport by hand, and rely on memory for which LTS lines require backports. This increases time-to-fix, causes inconsistent branch names, and occasionally leads to missing backports to customer-critical LTS channels. We need a deterministic process + tooling to reduce human error and shorten median time-to-repair for P0/P1 incidents.
proposed_solution: 1) Publish a triage matrix that maps incident symptoms to severity buckets (S0/S1/S2) and explicit backport targets. 2) Define a branch naming and patch-commit schema: patch/<release>-<yyyyMMdd>-<shortdesc>. 3) Implement a small CLI (release-propagate) that, given a canonical fix commit on main, will create patch branches on target release branches, run an automated preflight test suite, open draft PRs, and optionally merge after approvals. 4) Add a lightweight rollback hook that records propagation metadata and can revert propagated merges across releases with a single command.
acceptance_criteria: A triage matrix doc is published in Release Infra Confluence and linked in the on-call playbook
CLI release-propagate exists in repo release-scripts with tests and docs
Given a main commit hash, release-propagate can create patch branches and open draft PRs against main, stable-1.18, and lts-1.16
Preflight pipeline runs automatically on each draft PR and enforces a minimal test set (smoke + regression for affected component)
Automated metadata file is written to repo (propagation-record/<timestamp>.yaml) capturing commit/targets/author and used by rollback hook
Rollback command can revert merged propagation PRs across multiple release branches within one invocation and logs the revert PRs
rollout_gates: Severity mapping: S0 (security/availability/data loss) -> immediate propagation to all supported LTS and stable branches
S1 (high customer impact, degraded service) -> propagate to stable and active LTS only; require 1 release-engineer approval
S2 (low impact/behavioral) -> backport only if regression tests indicate real break and with scheduled minor release
Preflight gate: smoke tests + affected-component regression must pass before any merge
Approval gate: for S0 auto-merge allowed only after passing preflight and on-call signoff; for others require formal PR review
rollback_criteria: Customer-facing degradation within 30 minutes of propagation -> immediate rollback (invoke release-propagate rollback --record <id>)
Critical regression detected by canary or telemetry -> rollback triggered by release-engineer or SRE lead
Manual rollback must include post-rollback validation run and incident note authored in Confluence
Rollback process must not leave dangling cherry-picks: all propagation-record entries must be closed or annotated
test_plan: Unit tests covering branch creation, PR generation, and metadata recording
Integration test that runs a simulated propagation to a temporary branch with a subset of the preflight pipeline
End-to-end dry-run: run release-propagate --dry-run against staging to validate PR diffs and pipeline triggers
Post-merge smoke validation that runs full runtime-integration tests on a single replica using the propagated patch
Canary monitoring dashboard link for 1.18 and 1.16 to validate rollout health: https://grafana.redwood-internal/boards/rollouts
automation_details: Primary commands: release-propagate create --commit <sha> --targets stable-1.18,lts-1.16 --dry-run; release-propagate merge --id <prop-id> --auto-approve (S0 only)
Metadata file schema: propagation-record/<id>.md (YAML frontmatter in markdown) to keep audits searchable in git history
Auth: CLI uses GitHub App with repo scope; runs as automation user (bot-release) and records human approver in metadata
Safety: staged sleeps and rate limits between merges to avoid thundering merges across CI, with opt-out via --rush flag for emergency cases

notes: Trade-off: fully automated auto-merge for S0 reduces MTTR but increases blast radius; mitigations: strict preflight + on-call signoff
We intentionally model metadata as git-tracked records rather than external DB to preserve provenance and make reverts reproducible
This ticket targets runtime-1.18 and lts-1.16 for the initial rollout; broader coverage will follow after 2 weeks of stability
Related reading: internal RFC on LTS policy (link: https://redwood-internal.company/rfc/lts-policy)
